name: The Araucaria of Quinta Vigia

location.address: Quinta Vigia, Avenida do Infante 1, Se, Funchal

access: Free entry, government grounds (official residence of the President of the Regional Government of Madeira), open to the public Monday to Friday, roughly 08:00/08:30 to 17:30/18:00 depending on source; closed weekends and holidays. No appointment needed to walk the gardens.
transport: Avenida do Infante, central Funchal seafront; walkable (10-15 min) from Praca do Municipio, or a short bus/taxi ride. No car needed.
verify_notes: Officially designated as code 292 ("Araucaria") under Quinta Vigia in Quadro 5 of the Funchal PDM Relatorio de Fundamentacao (Volume II, March 2018), which itself cites the regional government publication "Arvores Monumentais e Emblematicas" (Direcao Regional de Florestas, 2008) as the source of the whole monumental-tree list for the municipality (118 specimens recensed, 111 monumental + 7 emblematic) -- one official register source. Second source: IFCN Madeira and visitmadeira.com/lifecooler.com independently confirm Quinta Vigia is a real, currently operating public garden (c.10,000 sqm), the official residence of the President of the Regional Government since 1984, open to the public free of charge on weekdays; these describe the garden and its general planting (which includes multiple araucaria and other exotic species) rather than this specific tree, so flagged as site-level corroboration, the same caveat already used on mdr_001-004 in this city file. SPECIES CAUTION: Wikidata (Q98858620) labels this specific specimen Araucaria columnaris but cites ZERO references for that claim; its own "described at" link points to a monumentaltrees.com page (height 41.20m, measured 2018-02-09) that this pass could not view (Cloudflare bot-check blocked both a plain fetch and a browser-session attempt, two tries). Per the search-summary rule, an unseen page is not evidence, so that height figure is NOT recorded here and the species is left at genus level rather than repeating an uncited claim -- the PDM table itself only says "Araucaria" with no species epithet, and IFCN prose about the garden separately mentions Araucaria heterophylla as one of several exotic species present at Quinta Vigia generally, so heterophylla vs columnaris is genuinely unresolved by this pass. The page should ask the reader which araucaria this is. Alive: garden in continuous active public/government use through 2026 per its own site and tourism sources. No girth or height recorded because the only figure found (monumentaltrees, via Wikidata) could not be verified on the source page itself.

name: The Ombu of the Municipal Garden

location.address: Jardim Municipal do Funchal, Rua Ivens 11, Se, Funchal

access: Free, public municipal garden, open every day (reported as open around the clock); this specific tree sits somewhere within an 8,300 sqm garden rather than at a marked spot.
transport: Central Funchal, Rua Ivens, a short walk from Avenida Arriaga and the seafront. No car needed.
verify_notes: Officially designated as code 305 ("Bela Sombra") under "Jardim Municipal do Funchal" in Quadro 5 of the Funchal PDM Relatorio de Fundamentacao (Volume II, March 2018), which cites the regional government publication "Arvores Monumentais e Emblematicas" (Direcao Regional de Florestas, 2008) as the source for the whole municipal monumental-tree list -- one official register source, same document used for mdr_007/009/010. Second source: the Portuguese Wikipedia article on the garden and the Camara Municipal do Funchal / visitfunchal pages independently confirm the Jardim Municipal do Funchal (formerly Jardim Dona Amelia, opened 1885 on the former Convento de Sao Francisco site) is a real, currently operating, free public garden at this exact address, bordered by Rua Ivens (north) and Rua Conselheiro Jose Silvestre Ribeiro (west), matching the Wikidata record street address for this tree; the Wikipedia article lists the garden general planting (barbusano, dragoeiro, til, pau-branco, kigelia, garcinia, plumeria, pandanus) but does not name the bela-sombra specifically, so flagged as site-level rather than tree-specific corroboration, same caveat pattern as the rest of this city file. LOCATION CAUTION: Wikidata gives the identical coordinate (32.647993,-16.912191) for BOTH this tree and the camphor tree (mdr_009) in the same garden, which reads as a single park-level point rather than two independently surveyed trunk positions, so both are marked approximate rather than confirmed. Garden is compact (8,300 sqm, roughly one hectare) so approximate still places a visitor within a short walk of the trunk. Alive: garden in continuous public use through 2026 per municipal and tourism sources. No girth or height found for this specific specimen; the parent 2008 survey likely records one but this pass could not access that book directly, only the PDM report that cites it. Species note: Phytolacca dioica is a South American species (Argentina/Uruguay/Brazil/Paraguay) unrelated to any Madeiran native, grown widely as a shade tree; the common Portuguese name means literally beautiful shade.

access: Free, public municipal garden, open every day (reported as open around the clock); this specific tree sits somewhere within an 8,300 sqm garden rather than at a marked spot.

name: The Pohutukawa of Quinta do Palheiro Ferreiro

location.address: Quinta do Palheiro Ferreiro (Palheiro Gardens), Caminho do Palheiro 32, Sao Goncalo, Funchal

access: Paid entry (Palheiro Gardens): adults EUR 11, ages 15-17 EUR 6, children free, Madeira residents EUR 6 with proof of residence; open daily 09:00-17:00, every day of the year except Christmas Day.
transport: Caminho do Palheiro, in the hills east of Funchal (about 500m altitude); reachable by taxi or car, roughly 15-20 minutes from central Funchal, or bus toward Sao Goncalo/Camacha plus a walk.
verify_notes: Officially designated as code 192 ("Metrosidero") under "Quinta do Palheiro, Palheiro Ferreiro" in Quadro 5 of the Funchal PDM Relatorio de Fundamentacao (Volume II, March 2018), the same document and 2008 regional source used for mdr_007/008/009; Wikidata (Q98815233) cites this exact PDM PDF as its own reference, confirming the match. Second source: TripAdvisor and madeira-web.com independently confirm Quinta do Palheiro Ferreiro (Palheiro Gardens) is a real, currently operating, paid private estate garden open daily, admired for its exotic plant collection; they describe the garden generally and do not name this specific metrosideros, so flagged as site-level rather than tree-specific corroboration, same caveat as the rest of this pass and the existing city file. ACCESS: private estate but genuinely open to the paying public every day (except Christmas), which satisfies the access test the same way Madeira paid-entry hard rule cases already do (e.g. the Botanical Garden ginkgo, mdr_001); this is not a private residence closed to visitors. Note the same PDM table lists SEVERAL other named specimens at this same Quinta do Palheiro / Palheiro Ferreiro location (tulipeiro, til, another araucaria da Queenslandia, carvalho, cedro do Atlas, another canforeira, nucleos de platanos, sequoia, pinheiro das canarias) under separate codes, so this is one specimen among many monumental trees in the same garden, picked as the collectible point for this pass because Metrosideros excelsa (pohutukawa) is a striking and distinctive New Zealand species rarely seen on this list; a second visit could add more from the same garden as separate entries later. Alive: garden in continuous paid public operation through 2026 per current tourism sources. No girth or height found for this specific specimen; the parent 2008 survey likely records one but this pass could not access that book directly.
